newsitem.title: USA: EuroMed to take loss on sale of Pluripharm.
newsitem.headline: EuroMed to take loss on sale of Pluripharm.

text.p: EuroMed Inc said it has entered a pact to sell its Pluripharm division to a pharmacy wholesale management group in The Netherlands for about $2.8 million, taking a loss of about $3.2 million on the sale.
The company did not disclose the name of the buyer.
Additionally, the company said its chairman, Francois Hinnen will return 850,000 shares of the company's stock upon closing of the sale.

The company said it also has a pact with Pluripharm's two former owners, A. Doets and N.T.P. Roozekrans, to indemnify them from third parties claims in exchange for 850,000 EuroMed shares they received when they sold Pluripharm.
The company said its board has also authorized a buy-back program of up to 300,000 shares of its common stock from time to time.
EuroMed said the moves would cut its outstanding common to about two million shares from four million shares.
The company's general counsel, Richard Dahlson, said Hinnen is giving 850,000 shares back to the company at no cost.

EuroMed, a wholesaler of about 6,000 pharmaceutical products with about $35 million in 1996 sales, bought Pluripharm, a pharmaceutical wholesaler in The Netherlands, in July 1996. EuroMed paid about $5.87 million cash and 850,000 in common shares valued at 6.75 a share for the company, said EuroMed board member Greg Gaylor.
Gaylor is seeking to fight the sale of the division.
The company's former chief financial officer, Jan Bouwman, said in a telephone interview from The Netherlands that the division was profitable in 1995 and in the first nine months of 1996.
The company's shares were delisted from Nasdaq in December.
EuroMed shares were off 1/8 Tuesday at 1-1/8.
